## Introduction

This vignette demonstrates how to programmatically design, manipulate, and validate a controlled 2x2 visual experiment using `neuroconsumer`.

### 1. Build Reference Stimulus

```r
bg <- nc_component("bg", type = "background", width = 1, height = 1, properties = list(fill = "#F8FAFC"))
brand <- nc_component("brand", type = "brand", x = 0.5, y = 0.1, properties = list(text = "LUMINA"))
headline <- nc_component("headline", type = "headline", x = 0.5, y = 0.22, properties = list(text = "Clarity Redefined"))
product <- nc_component("product", type = "product", x = 0.5, y = 0.45, width = 0.4, height = 0.3)
price <- nc_component("price", type = "price", x = 0.5, y = 0.65, properties = list(text = "$149.00"))
cta <- nc_component("cta", type = "cta", x = 0.5, y = 0.82, properties = list(text = "Order Now", fill = "#94A3B8"))

stim <- nc_stimulus("ref_ad", list(bg, brand, headline, product, price, cta))
exp <- nc_experiment("ad_study", reference = stim)
```

### 2. Declare Manipulations

```r
exp <- nc_manipulate(exp, factor = "price_pos", component = "price",
                     parameter = "y", levels = c(upper = 0.60, lower = 0.72))
exp <- nc_manipulate(exp, factor = "cta_contrast", component = "cta",
                     parameter = "properties.fill", levels = c(low = "#94A3B8", high = "#E11D48"))
```

### 3. Verify Experimental Invariants

```r
rep <- nc_validate(exp)
print(rep)
```
